q1_issues.issue: (Member sk_group_1 hopeful) predicates a copular property of the group symbol, which the instruction set explicitly forbids — a copular predicate on a plural must go through the per-member distribution rule.
(For sk_preference_1 sk_achieve_1) names an oblique after a preposition that never occurs in the text ('our preference IS TO achieve …'), so the head has no surface word licensing it.
The sealed complement of 'hopeful' is the bare status atom (Can sk_achieve_1), whose event class and role atoms sit outside the seal, so the sealed term is not a self-contained proposition.
'remain' is dropped entirely — nothing records the continuation of the hopeful state (no Still/Ongoing and no reified 'remain' event).
The appositive typing (Member marce_fuller chief_executive) is not wrapped in the host clause's past tense, though an appositive is specified to take the host clause's wrapper.

q2_gaps: direct quotation as the complement of a speech verb ("…," X said): the attitude section covers finite that-clauses only, and nothing states whether a verbatim quote is sealed, kept as a string literal, or both
specificational copular with an infinitival complement ('our preference is to achieve X') — no encoding for 'N is to V'
continuative copular verbs ('remain / stay ADJ') — no operator for the continuation, and the reification triggers do not include one
an adjective with a finite clausal complement ('hopeful (that) we can do so') — only an adjective's PP complement is covered
first- and second-person pronouns ('our', 'we', 'I', 'you') — the anonymous-witness rule classes he/she/it/they only, and nothing licenses linking the speaker into a 'we' group
notes: The name/title split (lowercase 'chief executive' as a separate type atom, symbol and Name string from the capitalized run) and the financial_restructuring genus + adjectival-modifier decomposition follow the instruction set, as does OutOf for the multi-word surface preposition. 'out of court' is attached to the restructuring entity rather than to the achieving event, which is the reading the sentence favours.
